devices.name: Metonymy
devices.definition: Naming something by a word closely associated with it — cause for effect, container for contents, author for writings.

occurrences.note: " I will scatter a third part into all the winds ": i.e., into all quarters
"The sword (i.e., war, or destruction) is without."
" The prince shall be clothed with desolation ": i.e., with his garments rent, which was the sign of his mourning. IV. Metonymy of the
"Ye have... strengthened the hands of the wicked, that he should not return from his wicked way, by quickening him": i.e., by promising him life
9). — " Seeing then that I will cut off from the righteous and the wicked." Here it is probably Metonymy, i.e., those who were reputed as righteous, but were not so. See verse 3 (8
"Yet she multiplied her whoredoms, in calling to remembrance the days of her youth, wherein she had played the harlot in the land of Egypt ": i.e., in desiring again the former sins
Strength is put for that which it effects or produces
" The desire of thine eyes ": i.e., thy wife, who is the object of thy desire
" They of the house of Togarmah ": i.e., of Togarmah's descendants
"And thou shalt say unto rebellion": i.e., to the rebellious People

devices.name: Anthropopatheia
devices.definition: Ascribing to God human feelings, parts, or actions, by way of condescension to us.

occurrences.note: "And I will be comforted." Jealousy
Hiding, for protection and defence
"All the heathen shall see my judgment that I have executed, and my hand that I have laid upon them." So Job
It is used of the Divine presence in anger and judgment

devices.name: Ellipsis
devices.definition: A word or words deliberately left out, to be supplied by the reader — compression and force.

occurrences.note: " This city shall not be your caldron, neither shall ye be the flesh in the midst thereof; but I will judge you [scattered] in the border of Israel."
" His boughs are broken by all the rivers of the land."
" The rivers shall be full of thee."
" And feed them upon the mountains of Israel by the rivers."
"Joseph shall hare two portions," i.e., shall inherit

devices.name: Epanadiplosis
devices.definition: A clause encircled — beginning and ending with the same word.

devices.name: Epizeuxis
devices.definition: Immediate repetition of a word for intense emphasis, with nothing between (“Lord, Lord”).

occurrences.note: " Wilt thou judge, wilt thou judge ? ": i.e., Wilt thou really and truly judge ?
" Turn ye, turn ye from your evil ways."

devices.name: Idiom
devices.definition: A peculiar usage of the Hebrew or Greek that does not carry its literal force — an idiom to be rendered by its sense, not word for word.

occurrences.note: " If the prophet be deceived when he hath spoken a thing, I the Lord have deceived that prophet ": i.e., I have permitted him to deceive himself
" Wherefore I gave them also statutes that were not good ": i.e., I permitted them to follow the wicked statutes of the surrounding nations, mentioned and forbidden
" To walk " is used for proceeding happily and prosperously
"According to the vision that I saw when I came to destroy the city,"

devices.name: Synecdoche
devices.definition: Substituting a part for the whole, or the whole for a part (“all the world”; “flesh and blood”).

occurrences.note: " Behold, therefore, I have stretched out my hand over thee and have diminished thy statute ": i.e., the food apportioned to thee. A.V.: "ordinary food."
J as. i. 27. — " Pure religion and undefiled before God and the Father is this, To visit the fatherless and widows in their affliction,"
"At the same time shall things ascend upon thine heart ": i.e., as in A.V., come into thy mind
" And it shall come to pass in the day of Gog's coming against the land of Israel,"

devices.name: Rhetorical question
devices.definition: A question asked for effect, not for an answer — to affirm, deny, or provoke thought.

devices.name: Paronomasia (wordplay)
devices.definition: A play on words that sound alike but differ in sense — pun, rhyme, near-repetition.

devices.name: Heterosis
devices.definition: Exchange of one grammatical form for another — of tense, number, person, degree, or mood (e.g. a future used for a command).

occurrences.note: "The city of the bloods": i.e., the city where so much blood has been shed
"Vengeances": i.e., great or terrible vengeance

devices.name: Personification
devices.definition: Giving human traits, action, or speech to something impersonal or abstract.

occurrences.note: " Cast ye away every man the abominations of his eyes."

devices.name: Hysteresis
devices.definition: A later passage supplying a detail not recorded in the earlier narrative it refers to.

devices.name: Pleonasm
devices.definition: A deliberate redundancy — more words than strictly needed — to underline or solemnise.

occurrences.note: " He shall not live: he hath done all these abominations; he shall surely die." Here, the negative is put first, and then repeated in the positive form
" Thou art a man, and not God."

devices.name: Polyptoton
devices.definition: Repetition of the same root word in different inflections (“dying you shall die”).

occurrences.note: " A king of kings ": i.e., the most mighty king
" To take a spoil, and to take a prey." Lit., to spoil spoil and to prey prey; i.e., to take great spoil and a great prey

devices.name: Ecphonesis
devices.definition: An outcry of feeling — a sudden exclamation breaking from strong emotion (“O the depth!”).

occurrences.note: " I fell upon my face, and cried, and said, Ah Lord God (Adonai Jehovah) ! "

devices.name: Irony
devices.definition: Saying the opposite of what is meant, so the real sense is felt through the contrast.

occurrences.note: " Go, shut thyself within thine house." But the 25th verse shows that however closely he might shut himself up his enemies should find him and bind him
"As for you, O house of Israel, thus saith the Lord Goo; Go ye, serve ye every one his idols,"
" Behold, thou art wiser than Daniel; there is no secret that they can hide from thee." God thus ironically addresses the king of Tyre. Daniel, on account of Divine gifts, was esteemed most wise

devices.name: Parable
devices.definition: A continued simile — a narrative laid alongside a truth to teach it by comparison.

devices.name: Periphrasis
devices.definition: Circumlocution: a description put in place of the plain name of a thing.

devices.name: Amphibologia
devices.definition: A saying deliberately capable of two meanings, both intended.

devices.name: Asyndeton
devices.definition: Conjunctions omitted between items in a series, producing a rapid, piled-up effect.

devices.name: Epistrophe
devices.definition: The same word or phrase ends a run of successive clauses (the mirror of anaphora).

devices.name: Hyperbole
devices.definition: Deliberate exaggeration, not meant literally, that drives a point home vividly.

occurrences.note: " Lose the life " is used of esteeming it as a small matter

devices.name: Hypotyposis
devices.definition: Vivid word-painting that sets a scene before the eyes as though present.

devices.name: Parallelism
devices.definition: Successive lines echo one another in structure — saying the same thing twice, or balancing matched clauses.

devices.name: Paroemia (proverb)
devices.definition: A proverb — a wayside-saying in common use, cited or coined.

devices.name: Anabasis
devices.definition: A gradual ascent — a series that mounts, clause by clause, to a high point.

devices.name: Anaphora
devices.definition: The same word or phrase begins a run of successive clauses, hammering a theme.

devices.name: Catabasis
devices.definition: A gradual descent — a series that steps down, clause by clause, to a low point (opposite of climax).

devices.name: Dialogismus
devices.definition: The speaker dramatises a dialogue, putting words into another's mouth.

devices.name: Enigma
devices.definition: A dark saying — a truth wrapped in obscure or riddling terms.

occurrences.note: gives a prophecy concerning the King of Babylon's coming to Jerusalem, and leading it into captivity, under the Enigma of two Eagles

devices.name: Epitheton
devices.definition: Naming a thing by an attribute or adjunct added to it (“John the Baptist”).

occurrences.note: An hand-breadth is used as an Epithet for a certain thickness

devices.name: Gnome (quotation)
devices.definition: A quotation or proverbial maxim woven in — a pithy saying cited for authority or point.

devices.name: Hypallage
devices.definition: Interchange: a word logically belonging to one term is grammatically attached to another.

devices.name: Maledictio
devices.definition: An imprecation or pronouncement of woe (“Woe to you…”).

devices.name: Merism
devices.definition: Naming the parts, or the two extremes, to mean the whole — “heaven and earth,” “your going out and your coming in.”

occurrences.note: After saying " Ye mountains of Israel, hear the word of the Lord God (Adonai Jehovah)," the word is spoken, not only to the mountains, but to the hills and rivers, and valleys, and desolate wastes

devices.name: Mesarchia
devices.definition: The same word repeated at both the beginning and the middle of successive clauses.

devices.name: Metaphor
devices.definition: An implied comparison that calls one thing another (“A is B”), without “like” or “as.”

devices.name: Polyonymia
devices.definition: Heaping up several different names or titles for the same person or thing.

devices.name: Simile
devices.definition: An explicit comparison of two unlike things using “like” or “as.”

occurrences.note: The gentile. We must not separate what God has joined together, nor join together what God has separated
